subject: Literature
title: Uncle Tom's Cabin and Abolitionism
description: Learn Uncle Tom's Cabin and Abolitionism in one minute.

hook.text: Abraham Lincoln reportedly told Harriet Beecher Stowe that her little book started the great Civil War.

buildup.text: Uncle Tom's Cabin depicted the horrors of slavery so vividly that it turned Northern opinion firmly against the practice.

discovery.text: It became the best-selling novel of the nineteenth century, second only to the Bible in American sales.

twist.text: Southern states banned the book, and in some places, possessing a copy could lead to imprisonment or violence.

climax.text: The banning proved that fiction can be a political weapon powerful enough to threaten an entire economic system.

punchline.text: A novel helped end slavery in the most powerful nation on Earth.

quiz.question: How did Southern states respond to Uncle Tom's Cabin?
options: They praised it as an accurate portrayal
They banned it and possession could lead to imprisonment
